description: The registry work type says the record is not a paper: a dataset, a software record, a database entry, a component or a supplementary object. Wrong entry type for FLoRA: not a report of a study — whatever such a record is the artifact OF, the record itself is not a study report and cannot become a FLoRA row. It sits above admission because these records carry their parent's phrases — a deposit titled "Replication Data for: …" fires admission arms while offering nothing to screen. Some of these records do carry description text, so this is a type claim, not a no-text claim. `component` and `database` are the two worth a second look (D4): a `component` can occasionally be an independently meaningful report. The residual risk is real: where a deposit is the ONLY record of a replication, that replication is lost. The mitigation would be a linkage worklist rather than an admission — record the deposit's parent DOI, check whether the parent is in the pool, route the unlinked remainder to a human — a separate open issue (#157).

measured.rationale: Structural and scope, not statistical: every type on this list is a registry vocabulary term for a record that is not a paper, and the discard claims exactly that — wrong entry type, not off-topic and not text-free. A precision sample would answer a different question (how often such an object is the artifact OF a replication), which the scope ruling (maintainer, 2026-08-04) deliberately does not turn on. What a sample IS still owed for is the residual loss — the deposit that is the only record of its replication — a separate open issue (#157, parent recovery per proposal SS7). Supersedes the retired `dataset-type` spec, whose 2026-08-03 pilot evidence measured screen spend (69.8% of dataset rows proceed in the concept arm vs 12.5% for articles) rather than precision and therefore could not license a live discard.
